questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose NYU mainly because I heard that the courses were on a very high level and that you could learn a lot from some very skilled professors. I also chose this location because I'm very interested i New York City with its opportunities and diverse cultures.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It was hard to get to know people at first, I think NYU could have done more in the beginning to make sure exchange students get to know each other. When you have a network of people it's much easier live and study there.
I really liked the courses, and the teachers. They all seems interested in their students and very competent in their field.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy enough to find information about courses. It wasn't that easy to find information about social events, NYU could have made that more accessible.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a mandatory intro day (which I wish their were more of), we also had some guidance counselors who we could write emails to or meet in person, which worked really well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was easy enough to find information about courses. It wasn't that easy to find information about social events, NYU could have made that more accessible.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was hard to find affordable housing which was also a good place to live. I found it through Airbnb and later I found a nicer place through some friends. I would recommend to anyone trying to find housing in New York to find a place close to metro station (preferably were you only have to take one line to get to your university) and a place that is close to a Trader Joe's or a Target since since common supermarkets are really expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is better to live somewhere where you either know people in advance or a place where there seem to be some kind of community. Airbnbs ain't always great since people move in and out and therefore most people were not that interested in getting to know each other.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Dorms are a great alternative, but there's no guarantee that you'll get along with your roommate or have a very close relationship to them. Also most of the dorms are in pretty run-down buildings.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It went pretty smoothly.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I got lots of emails describing how to set up an online account, and I went to the office to get my ID-card.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Guidance counselors and specific offices.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, I also managed to swap two course after I tried one course and found out it wasn't for me.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Write an email to a guidance counselors if you're in doubt of something.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found that the academic level at NYU isn't as theoretically based as it is at my home university. It's more practical.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All courses were undergrad level courses. Some were very beginner level other were more advanced.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In the US your verbal participation in class can affect your grade. This means that a lot of student say something in class, which can lead to some interesting discussions but it also leads to a lot of noise - students just saying something because they know they have to. You can always talk to your teachers about this and what they expect of you in class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Fundamentals of Filmmaking I
Acting for the camera
Transgender Youth
Intro to Psychology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Acting for the camera - the course is great whether you want to work in front or behind the camera or if you just want to try something completely different to your other courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Food is very expensive because of inflation, housing is too, clothes and visiting famous landmarks is as well - actually everything is expensive in New York :) 
The NYU insurance was insanely expensive. I later found out that you can get it cheaper elsewhere.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food, housing and clothes is more expensive.
You can get a reduced price at certain sights and museums with student discounts.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: You can read about all of them and figure out what's interesting for you

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit the famous landmarks, try out different restaurants and fastfood places

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was harder than I thought. New York is a very loud city with lots of yelling and there's a certain over-politeness that can seem kind of fake from a scandinavian point of view.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sadly most local students are not that interested in a deep relationship with exchange students since they know they won't be there for long. You can get lucky though and meet some American students who are interested, but mostly you'll hang out with other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
One thing that was very particularly hard to adjust to was the inequality. There's a lot of poor people living on the street and the problem has only grown bigger since covid. It can be pretty heartbreaking to witness.

Other than that there's the loudness, lots of people yell all the time, also during normal conversations. People often get very mad at each other but I've never witnessed violence, people just let out a lot of steam.

It's very hard to get close to locals, but it makes sense in a city were people quickly jump from one thing to the next.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The magnitude of everything, the buildings, the sights and also the mixture of different cultures you can experience.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Find a place close to a metro and affordable supermarkets.
Find a community of people you like and trust otherwise New York City can feel quite lonely.
Make you to explore the city and play turist once in a while, then you're living in a city and are busy studying or working sometimes you might forget how great it is.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you're having trouble finding a community I can recommend trying to find some other danish people living in New York on Facebook groups. Even if your initial idea was not to hang out with other danish it actually helps a lot to share your weird New York experience (both the good and the bad) with someone from back home who are experiencing the same as you.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Showing my films in class and getting people's reactions.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding an affordable place to stay (moved 3 times)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
